chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Ali ibn Ma'bad from al-Husayn ibn Khalid from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, peace be upon him.

He said: Looking at our offspring is worship. So, it was said to him: O son of the Messenger of God! Is looking at the Imams from among you worship, or looking at all the offspring of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family? So, he said: Rather, looking at all the offspring of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, is worship.

key_terms.النَّظَرُ: Looking/gazing; here a respectful, contemplative gaze upon the descendants of the Prophet as a form of devotion
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: The Imams; the divinely appointed leaders from the Prophet's household
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّةِ النَّبِيِّ: Offspring of the Prophet; all biological descendants of Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّتِنَا: Our offspring; the descendants of the Prophet and Ahl al-Bayt, including all Sayyids
key_terms.عِبَادَةٌ: Worship; an act of devotion to God, here elevating the gaze upon Prophetic descendants to worship status

ai.seo_question: Is looking at the descendants of the Prophet Muhammad an act of worship according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam al-Rida (AS) declares that looking at the Prophet's offspring is an act of worship. When asked whether this applies only to the Imams or to all descendants of the Prophet (SAWW), he clarifies that it encompasses all of the Prophet's descendants without distinction. This teaching was delivered in the context of the immense spiritual status afforded to the Prophetic lineage, reflecting the Quranic injunction to love the Prophet's near relatives (42:23). The original audience understood this as an affirmation that reverence for all Sayyids is spiritually meritorious.
